title: Composing like cycles tests codes for linearity and certifies tractability with constants
subject: What the composition characterization is good for, and whether it was already known
conclusion: No statement of the composition characterization turned up in a bounded literature scan; its uses are a composition test for linearity of codes, under which the non-Pappus almost affine code fails through an explicit three-copy system, and a tractability certificate for laws that keep composing like cycles with constants. Counting is not covered, and constants can destroy composing like cycles, so whether every such law is tractable is open.
